questions.question: What is "bilateral aid"?
options: Aid given directly from one government to another
Aid given by private companies only
Aid that must be repaid with interest
questions.explanation: Bilateral aid is given directly from one government to another; multilateral aid is channelled through international organisations.

questions.question: Why is "tied aid" generally considered less effective than "untied aid"?
options: It requires recipients to buy from the donor country, reducing value
It gives recipients too much freedom
It is always larger in amount
It is given only in emergencies
questions.explanation: Tied aid requires purchases from the donor country, so it is generally less effective than untied aid that seeks best value.

questions.question: Approximately what share of its national income does Norway spend on foreign aid?
questions.explanation: Norway typically spends about 1% of GNI on official development assistance — one of the highest proportions in the world.

questions.question: Which economist argues that aid can break the "poverty trap"?
questions.explanation: Jeffrey Sachs argues extreme poverty is a trap that well-targeted aid can break; Moyo and Easterly are more critical.

questions.question: According to the emerging consensus, aid works best when:
options: Combined with good governance, local ownership, trade and investment
Given with no conditions or measurement
questions.explanation: The emerging consensus is that aid works best alongside good governance, local ownership, trade and careful measurement of results.
